name: Are Right, A Lot
definition: Leaders are right a lot. They have strong judgment and good instincts. They seek diverse perspectives and work to disconfirm their beliefs.

rows.justRight: Keeps gathering the relevant data and still sets direction.
rows.over: Treats today's right answer as permanent. Does not notice when the facts have moved.

rows.situation: Committing when the picture is incomplete
rows.justRight: Stays current on the business. Uses trends and evidence to make a consistent, informed call.
rows.over: Charges ahead with a blind spot. Ignores {lp:invent-and-simplify}. Optimizes the company at the cost of the people who have to live with the call.

rows.under: May not be right, but fakes a recommendation anyway.
rows.justRight: Drives to a resolution despite uncertainty. Says what is known, what is a guess, and why this path.
rows.over: May be right, and browbeats the room. Needs to be the smartest person present.

rows.situation: Guiding a team without taking the work
rows.under: Does not guide enough. The team makes expensive wrong calls or invents a costly process.
rows.justRight: Sets a clear direction, simplifies the work, and generates the same behavior downstream.
rows.over: Freezes the team with too much direction. Kills {lp:ownership}.

rows.situation: Hearing the team, then calling it
rows.under: Does not use data. Makes a hasty call that sends the team down the wrong path.
rows.justRight: Takes input and data from the team and regularly makes the right call.
rows.over: Makes every decision and will not listen. Unaware of blind spots. Disempowers the people closest to the work.

rows.situation: Confusing this principle with always being right
rows.under: Undervalues their own experience. Never establishes respect.
rows.justRight: Knows "a lot" is not "always." Seeks input and applies experience. Champions the best path even when it was not theirs.
rows.over: Mistakes this principle for always being right. Will not integrate an outside view.

rows.situation: How much you need to know before you act
rows.under: Decides on insufficient or flawed knowledge.
rows.justRight: Knows enough to take a well-informed, calculated risk.
rows.over: Gets paralyzed by the need to know everything. Unable to act.

rows.situation: When the team should own the call
rows.under: Not in tune with whether the team is making right decisions.
rows.justRight: Knows when the team is on or off track. Lets them act without micromanaging.
rows.over: Unable to let others be right.

rows.situation: Standing behind a decision you made
rows.under: Decides from third-party information they do not actually understand.
rows.justRight: Makes conscientious, well-considered decisions they can explain from first principles.
rows.over: Rationalizes when challenged. Or avoids deciding so they cannot be wrong.

rows.situation: Balancing the long term and the short term
rows.under: Uses fuzzy long-term language to excuse a badly thought-out project, or optimizes this month and leaves the root cause in place.
rows.justRight: Balances long-term and short-term on purpose, and can say which one this call is for.
rows.over: Will not make a reasonable judgment call because they are hunting the perfect long-term solution.

rows.under: Seeks too much collaboration and affirmation before they will move.
rows.justRight: Invites challenge. Comfortable deciding with directional data. Stays accountable when they miss.
rows.over: Gets defensive when shown an opposing view. Lacks humility.
